welcomeText: The Witness Isles remember those who have proven themselves. So do I. Ask about the "rite" if you wish to be reborn.

topics.response: The Witness Isles' pact is stirring. Stand against the Fey Wardens that still test it, then return at full strength. Ask about the "rite" again when you are ready.
Once the Witness Isles have seen your proof, ask me for "rebirth". You need not return to the Oracle.
I thought the Oracle's trial was the only door left. The Witness Isles kept another. Ask about the "rite".

welcomeText: Archmage Thalindra. The Witness Isles sit on old ley lines. Name a school - fire, water, earth, air, dark or light - and I will show you what it holds.

topics.response: Veilstone Aegis, Wellspring Mercy, Leyward Bastion, Dawnwell Renewal - the ley-line wards and mercies. For the killing arts, name a school: fire, water, earth, air, dark or light.
The Wilds' fey draw on the same ley lines I do, gentler than my own working. That kinship is the only reason they still tolerate a tower full of spellbooks in their woods.

The high arts were never meant to be taught lightly. Every school offers the same five rungs - at the hundred-and-fiftieth level, then every fifty levels after, up to the three-hundred-and-fiftieth - and each rung demands a mind to match it. Come back when you're ready.

The apex of every school is the same distance up the ladder: the three-hundred-and-fiftieth level, and a mind of eight hundred and seventy-five in its governing art. Name a school and I'll show you the whole climb.
Scorchbrand, Pyreburst, Magmaheart Lance, Sunforge Brand, Emberqueen's Wrath - the pyromancer's ladder. Fire answers to Intelligence.
Rime Lance, Frostgale, Abyssal Spear, Tidebreaker, Drowning Deep - the tidecaller's ladder. Water answers to Intelligence.
Stonefang, Land Slide, Gravebreaker, Mountain's Fist, Worldroot Upheaval - the geomancer's ladder. Earth answers to Wisdom.
Galespike, Thunderhead, Skysplitter, Tempest Lance, Stormcaller's Judgment - the windweaver's ladder. The storm asks for Intelligence and Wisdom in equal measure.
Nightfang, Shadowblight, Soulrend, Voidreave Lance, Umbral Tide - the shadowmancer's ladder. Darkness answers to Intelligence.
Sunscour, Dawnflare, Radiant Spear, Seraph's Verdict, Hallowed Nova - the lightbringer's ladder. Light answers to Wisdom.

Every master of a school should wear its colors. Ember red, tide blue, verdant green, storm gold, shadow black, dawn white - woven on the ley lines themselves, and they will only settle on the shoulders of a caster of real standing.

welcomeText: Ophira has exposed the wound in the Witness Isles. I can guide you through two accounts of its cause. Ask "witnesses", "warders", or "hierarchy" to learn more.

topics.response: Ask me for the "story".
Say "accept" when you are ready.
Say "report" when the deed is done.
Say "route" for the marked location.
Ask about "witnesses".
Ask about "warders".
Say "moonwake" to choose this account.
Say "emberglass" to choose this account.
Ask about "hierarchy".
Ask about "threnody".
Ask for the "epilogue" after the final report.

welcomeText: The crossing to Kraanhold isn't a pleasant one. Clear the road trolls harassing the coast first, and I'll see you safely across.

topics.response: Trolls have been working the coast road east of here for longer than I've kept this dock. Thin their numbers and I'll take you across to Kraanhold myself - can't risk the boat with them still raiding the shore.
Kraanhold. A stretch of coast and mountain out past the shoals - centaurs hold the marches, and it only gets worse from there. Drakes, they say, further up in the peaks.
Nothing clever about them, just big and mean. They've gotten bold enough to block the coast road entirely some days.
Watch the tide line. I've lost more than one boat to trolls wading out after it.

welcomeText: Welcome to Witness Isles Sanctuary. I am Elder Ophira. Our loyal fey hold the northern wilds while corruption spreads from the Veil. Ask about the "wilds" to learn how you can help.

topics.response: The Witness Wilds lie north of the sanctuary. Moonlit Stalkers hunt in two clearings along the route. The fey still honor our pact; protect them. Ask "route" for directions.
The Fading Veil lies south of the sanctuary. Ysolde's wraiths spread the blight from her ruined court. After the Wilds, this is our next struggle.

Sir Caradoc was once the truest knight our isle ever raised. Ysolde bound his spirit to her service. He haunts the border glade west of the sanctuary. His sundered blade is rare loot, not proof required for the vigil.
Ysolde was no matriarch of ours. She came veiled, in peace, and left the corruption that now bears her name. She is the source of the blight, not merely its steward.
The Verdant Warden is the last of the old treant guardians still standing his ground against the blight. He answers to no one, not even us - but he has not fallen, and that alone gives us hope.
Ask about the wilds first. I will explain the task before you accept it. When the vigil is finished, we can turn our attention to the veil.
First ask me about the wilds, or the veil if you have already finished the vigil. Hear what must be done before you accept.
You have not accepted this task. Ask about the wilds to begin, or the veil after completing the vigil.

Leave the temple and follow the northbound road. The Stalker clearings lie northwest of us. Defeat them within the marked Wilds area, then return to report. Caradoc haunts the western border glade if you seek his rare blade.

welcomeText: The forge hasn't gone cold in longer than you'd believe. Neither have I, if it comes to that.

topics.response: Everyone thinks the old pact was words and nothing more. It wasn't - it was bound in metal too, once, and I still remember how. Bring me five embers torn from something that's already brushed against that kind of power, and I'll temper you a core worth building on.
I was young when the pact was still whole. I watched us bind it, and I watched us fail to keep it whole. Forging one more relic won't undo that - but it might buy the Wilds a little more time.

welcomeText: I am Soren, the last warder who refused the Marshal's new oath. Ask "testimony" about our betrayal, then "clue" about his chart.

topics.response: We swore to guard a prison, not worship its prisoner. The Marshal sold our names to the Dusk Regent, Rhunor's half-god, and received a chart that crosses forgotten water. You have broken his patrols; now I can expose his bargain. Ask "clue".

The Marshal carries the chart under his broken command seal. Defeat him at (4360,2630); the seal will release the route to Threnody. His oath answers to the Regent, not the bell. Return to Maelin at (4050,1480) and say "accept", then "route" for her instructions.

welcomeText: You've found the last of us. Say what you've come to forge, and I'll tell you if you've earned it yet.

topics.response: Bring me a tempered core and a bound sigil, and name the warblade - the rest is mine to finish.
A core, a sigil, and the will to loose something the old pact would have called a small storm. Bring the first two; I'll handle the rest.
Bring me a tempered core and a bound sigil, and I'll pour what's left of the old power into glass dark enough to hold it.
A core, a sigil, and a hand steady enough for both mind and heart to guide it. Bring me the first two.
This one's closer to my own heart than the rest. Bring me a core and a sigil, and I'll set what's left of the pact itself into a torc worth wearing.

Three of us are left who remember binding it whole. I don't know if forging pieces of it back into the world helps the original working or just delays the inevitable - but I'd rather try than watch it fray in silence.

welcomeText: Few make it this far and fewer still make it back. What do you need, champion?

topics.response: The Bastion Wardens have held that ruin for longer than anyone living remembers. Break enough of them and the old wards will finally weaken.
The Greater Drake sleeps at the bastion's heart. Every warden that falls is one less reason for it to stay asleep. Think on that before you wake it.
May whatever you worship still be listening where you're going.

welcomeText: Stonecrest's quay remembers every ship that failed to return. Ask me about the "isles" beyond the shoal, or why I still keep this dock. My "manifest" also connects these waters to missing names on the mainland. Ask "story" to follow that optional investigation.

topics.response: East of Stonecrest, Ithrak's Tideworn Reavers hold the only safe crossing to the Witness Isles. The last sailors who tried it lost more than their way: their families forgot their names. Ask about the "scouts" to prove you can face his warband, or ask "route" for directions.
Ask about the scouts to begin the first test.
Ask about Ithrak's chart after the scouts.
Return to me and report what happened.

Leave Stonecrest by the eastern road. The reavers gather near (420,730), and Ithrak keeps his command near (455,745). Bring his chart back to me. Say "scouts" to begin, then "report" when the first deed is done.
Ithrak was once a sworn coastwarden. Now he sells the crossing and keeps its "chart" for himself. Ask about the chart after you have faced his scouts.

The crossing is yours once the reavers are driven back and Ithrak's chart is returned. Use Locations to travel to Witness Isles Sanctuary, then ask Elder Ophira about the "wilds". Your passage remains open after rebirth.
The reavers patrol Stoneheim's road east of Stonecrest. Ask for the "route", then return and "report" each deed.
My son crossed without a chart. The tide took him, and for one night even I forgot his name. The old "pact" beyond the shoal is failing; I will not send another traveler blind.
The pact once kept the Witness Isles and Stoneheim from sharing the same wound. Its warders left us this road. Ask about the "scouts" if you mean to follow them.

A captain remembers paying a crew whose names have vanished from his manifest. Kilhiam in Lighthaven has another such account. Ask "story" to follow the mainland witnesses. When Thomas has compared their testimony at the Library, say "compare" here. The passage itself remains available through "isles".

The library account matches the spaces in my manifest. Your investigation now reaches the Witness Isles: mortal lives leave traces even as their names disappear. Ask "isles" about passage, "scouts" for the first deed, or "route" for the current voyage objective. Once across, ask Elder Ophira "wilds". You can always return and ask "story".
Ask "story" for the next speaker, destination and keyword in the missing-names investigation.

welcomeText: Five wyrms. Five scales. One seal that isn't a wyrm at all.

topics.response: Five Elder Wyrms sleep in Drake's Lair, and each of them sheds a scale, rarely, to whoever proves strong enough to earn one. Bring me all five - Rootcrown, Pyreclaw, Mistwing, Duskmaw, Galecrest - and I'll open the seal behind me. What answers isn't a sixth exemplar. It's what all five of them converge into.

welcomeText: Careful where you step. Something's been dragging people under since the tide turned.

topics.response: Deep Ones have been dragging travelers under all along this stretch of the coast. Thin their numbers and I'll see you paid for it.
There's a bigger one down there. The others answer to it. I wouldn't go looking for it without help.
Stay off the wet ground after dark. That's when they surface.

welcomeText: Maelin has sent another keeper of the oath. Whether you recovered the first bell or the betrayer's chart, the road ends here at Threnody Reach. Ask "story", or "hierarchy" to learn more.

topics.response: Ask me for the "story".
Say "accept" when you are ready.
Say "report" when the deed is done.
Say "route" for the marked location.
Ask about "witnesses".
Ask about "warders".
Say "moonwake" to choose this account.
Say "emberglass" to choose this account.
Ask about "hierarchy".
Ask about "threnody".
Ask for the "epilogue" after the final report.

welcomeText: The centaur warbands have been raiding out of the western marches again. Windhowl needs sellswords, not just soldiers.

topics.response: Centaur Warriors have been raiding the marches west of here, and their king rides with them now. Thin their ranks and Windhowl will pay you well for it.
Their king wears a crown he has no right to. Bring me his head and I'll see you rewarded beyond the usual bounty.
Resha still carries bows blessed for centaur-slaying, if the old stories are true. Ask her, not me.
Watch the tall grass. They ambush from it.

welcomeText: Look into the mirror, %s. It has been looking at you for a long time.

topics.response: This mirror has hung in the Colosseum longer than the Colosseum has had a name. When the Oracle - or the Witness Isles - remakes you, the life you shed doesn't simply vanish. Its echo settles here. Say echo, and yours will step out of the glass: your face, your gear, your spells, your strength. Win, and the mirror rewards you. Fall, and it takes nothing - it only wants to be seen.
Say echo and your reflection will step out to face you.
There are ten trials. Each echo is stronger than the last, and the first win of each trial pays well.
Once you've won all ten trials, your echo will walk beside you whenever you call it.
Me? I looked into the mirror once, a very long time ago, and I never quite stopped. Someone has to stay and make sure the echoes are seen.
Ask me about the letter, if one found its way to you.

welcomeText: I am Ilyra. The sea took my family's voices, but it has not taken their names. Ask "testimony" about the bell, then "clue" about its keeper.

topics.response: My sister rang the first bell while the warders bound Rhunor. The Pale Cantor stole her last note and made the drowned sing it forever. Now that you have freed their names, I can remember the bell's flaw. Ask "clue".

The Cantor hid the original note inside her Bell Shard. Defeat her at (4050,675) and recover it; the shard remembers Threnody even when every chart forgets. I entrust this memory to you. Return to Maelin at (4050,1480) and say "accept", then "route" for her instructions.

welcomeText: Thessaly gets the coin-counters. I get the ones who want something that lasts.

topics.response: Thessaly will pay you well for clearing this coast, and she should - that's fair work. But gold spends once. I've still got friends on Kraanhold's own docks, from before this coast forgot the crossing existed. Clear enough tolltrolls and I'll put in a word for you with them myself - one master or the other, not both. Which one you choose is yours to make.

welcomeText: Halvard. Windhowl's roads aren't as safe as they look - prove you can clear them before you go wandering the hills.

topics.response: Brigands have been working the roads north and east of town again, bolder than usual. Clear enough of them out and I'll know you can hold a line before you go looking for whatever's smoldering in those hills south of here.
South of here the hills catch fire on their own some nights - Cinderreach, we call it. A drake's made a den of it, or so the hunters who came back say.
Windhowl doesn't send its own out past the marches without knowing they can fight. The centaurs further out taught us that the hard way.
Deserters and opportunists, mostly. Nothing organized, just enough of them to make the roads dangerous for anyone traveling alone.

welcomeText: Turn back if you're not ready. What's past this ridge doesn't forgive.

topics.response: Kraanian Dragonguard hold the approach to the old drakes' lair, further out than anything we've mapped before. Cull enough of them and the Vigil will pay you well.
Something older than the Greater Drake sleeps past the guard line. The maps just call it the Arch Drake. I hope they're wrong.
Don't go past the guard line alone. I mean that as a warning, not a dare.

welcomeText: Quartermaster Elenna, at your service. If you mean to walk the Wilds or the Veil, you'll want better steel than you're carrying.

topics.response: Everything on this rack was forged or bought for Sanctuary's own garrison. It'll serve you just as well out there.
We hold this seam between the Wilds and the Veil. Lose the Sanctuary and both halves of the isle lose their only safe ground.
The Wilds are gentler than the Veil, but don't let that fool you - a Moonlit Stalker will still take your arm off.

welcomeText: Sorry, we're closed during the night and I'm off to bed.

topics.response: The name is Rhodar Heatforge but people usually call me Rhodar.
Yes, that's my name.
I am the weaponsmith of the village. I forge all my weapons myself from ore obtained in the mountains.
You want to buy something, is that it?

Wait a minute! Lemme see that hammer you have... hey, that's mine!!! How did you find it?! Ah.. Qardos.. that wretched blackguard... of course! If I was a bit younger, I swear I'd put this hammer to good use. Now, will you give it back to me?

Hey, you've killed %u goblins, right? Looks like you hate them as much as I do. Come with me in the back of the store, I've got something to show you that might be useful. Look at this beautiful sword, it's a Goblin Slayer sword. It has the uncanny ability of literally destroying goblins. It's yours if you're willing to pay the fair price of 25000 gold pieces. Does that sound fair to you?
The desert of "Vulture's" "Den" is nearly as hot as my forge. You shouldn't go there or I'll lose yet another good customer.
That's the name of the desert on the west part of the island.
What do you want to sell?
I would not go there if I were you. Unless you're wielding one of my great weapons of course.
Brownbark is a woodcutter who lives somewhere in Ravenwood with his son, Anrak.
Bane Blackblood wants to rule over the island of Raven's Dust but he won't as "King" "Theodore" "XIII"'s guards are using my weapons. *smile*
I heard he won the throne by sleeping. I wish I could do the same.
He is the orc leader.
Althea is the name of the world in which you are.
Do not be afraid to come back to my shop if you need anything else.
Ask me about goblins if you're hunting a bounty. I keep count same as everyone else on this island does.

welcomeText: I can take you straight to the Oracle's final trial. Ask about the "path"; choose "light" or "shadow", then say "trial" when you are ready.

topics.response: Choose "light" to face Gabriel Archonis or "shadow" to face Gaenen Elthorn. Your choice sets your karma and fixed alignment, affecting other conversations. Say "prepare" for the travel key and return scroll, then "trial" to enter the chamber. After victory, return and say "oracle".
Your path is light: your karma is now 100. Say "prepare" for the key and return scroll, then "trial" when ready to face Gabriel.
Your path is shadow: your karma is now -100. Say "prepare" for the key and return scroll, then "trial" when ready to face Gaenen.

I have arranged your Stoneheim passage and Oracle introduction, and given you a trial key and Stonecrest return scroll. Say "trial" to enter the final chamber. After victory, use the scroll and return to say "oracle".
Gabriel Archonis waits ahead. Survive his trial, then use the Stonecrest scroll to return and say "oracle".
Your victory is known. Speak to the Oracle and say "rebirth", then "ready to be reborn" to begin the rite.

welcomeText: Careful past the ridge, friend. The Cinderreach Hills have been smoking worse than usual.

topics.response: Ashfang Stalkers have been raiding the foothills in packs, and they're bolder every week. Cull enough of them and there's coin in it for you.
There's a drake denned up in the hills, one the Stalkers answer to. Ignarok, the old maps call him. I wouldn't go looking for him without a good blade.
I've traded a few fire workings off travelers over the years. Ask to TEACH if you've got the coin and the nerve.
Cinderreach used to be good grazing land, south of Windhowl. Now half of it's scorched black and the other half is smoking.
Watch the wind - it carries the smoke, and worse. Safe travels.

welcomeText: Corwin here. If you're heading east past the fields, best prove you can handle yourself first.

topics.response: The antelope herds past the fields have turned skittish and mean since the tide started acting up east of town - something's spooked them. Thin their numbers and I'll know you can hold your own before you go looking for whatever's actually wrong out there.

There's an old shrine out past the coast east of here - the Sunken Chancel, folk call it. Something's been dragging people under since the tide 'woke' it. Not my business until it comes ashore, but it will, eventually.
Silversky's held the coast a long time. We don't send folk out past the fields without knowing they can handle themselves first - too many haven't come back.
Nothing wrong with antelope, normally. Lately they're jumpier and meaner than they should be - had one take a chunk out of a fisherman's arm last week.

welcomeText: Peace to you, traveler. This temple stands open to anyone the Veil has bruised, whichever side of the seam you call home.

topics.response: This temple sits at the seam on purpose. Neither the Wilds nor the Veil can claim consecrated ground.
The Wilds still sing, if you know how to listen. I pray it stays that way.
I have prayed over the Veil's dead more times than I can count. None of my prayers have slowed it. Go carefully if you must go there at all.

welcomeText: You hear the wyrmlings before you see them. If you can hear the Drake itself, you're already too close.

topics.response: Kraanian Wyrmlings have nested in the aerie east of here, and something far older sleeps above them. Thin the nest and I'll pay you from my own purse.
A true Drake hasn't been seen on this island in a generation. I've spent that long proving the old maps right.
Fly low, or don't fly at all. That's the only advice I have for you.
I can teach you Leyward Bastion, if you've the level and the mind for it - a ward that guards a whole party against the elements at once. Ask to TEACH.

welcomeText: Welcome. I can teach you nearly every spell known to this world. Say "learn" to see what I can teach you.
The tide brought something foul ashore near Silversky. Stand with me, or move along.

topics.response: Drowned Acolytes have been crawling out of the flooded chancel east of town, dragging folk under the waves. Thin their numbers and I'll see you paid.
Mordrenn was a priest once, before the tide claimed him. Now he calls himself an Inquisitor and holds court in the drowned chancel, judging anyone who wades too close.
I picked up a working or two studying the tide magic that keeps those cultists breathing underwater. Ask to TEACH if you want to learn.
Silversky's coast used to be calm. Since the chancel woke up, the fishing fleets won't sail past the old lighthouse without an escort.
Safe travels. Keep your boots dry.

welcomeText: The mirror asks who you were. I only ask how fast you are.

topics.response: Say trial and I'll set a Sandglass Sentinel against you - fixed strength, fixed health, no mirror tricks. Beat it, and the hourglass remembers your time. Beat your own best, and it's worth something. The tier rises the more times you've been remade, same as the mirror behind me.
Ask me for your times and I'll read every tier you've ever cleared.

welcomeText: The old wards over this temple don't hold themselves. Keep the dead from stirring at the grave markers east of town, and I'll see you rewarded with something worth knowing.

topics.response: Skeletons keep rising at the old grave markers east of the temple grounds, and every one that claws free saps a little more strength from the wards keeping this town safe. Put twelve of them back in the ground and I'll teach you how to renew your own wards in a single breath.
East, past the old grave markers - that's where the ground gave first. I don't know what stirred them, only that it hasn't stopped.

welcomeText: Don't linger past dusk here. The barrows wake at dark, and something crowned still walks among them.

topics.response: Wights have been crawling out of the old barrows south of the marches. Put them back down and I'll pay you from the March Watch's own coffer.
They call him the Hollow King. No one remembers which king he was in life. Whatever crowned him now isn't a kindness.
Keep your torch lit. It's the only mercy the barrows understand.

welcomeText: Careful where you stand. Whatever I'm binding doesn't always stay bound the first time.

topics.response: A core is only half of anything. Bring me five shards of aether - the kind that only forms where the veil between us and whatever's beyond it wears thin - and I'll bind you a sigil to match Corvain's work.
I've spent longer holding this pact together than I ever spent studying to help build it. Some nights I can't tell anymore whether I'm binding the shard or the shard's binding me.

welcomeText: Bryndis, wayfarer and scroll-trader. Buy a Scroll of the Witness Isles before you leave - you'll thank me the first time you need to get back here in a hurry.

topics.response: The Scroll of the Witness Isles carries you straight to the Sanctuary temple, no matter how far you've wandered. Cheap insurance, if you ask me.
The Witness Isles Gateway is the spell woven into that scroll. Ask Archmage Thalindra if you'd rather learn to cast it yourself.
I don't sell passage into the Veil. Nobody sane charters that road on purpose.
